To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Chinese state gained control of art and collecting in the 195os and 1960os by building state museums and co-opting conoisseurs, but that this control was not absolute.
The state gained control of collecting and connoisseurship in Shanghai by building museums and co-opting collectors, while some illegal trade continued outside of official institutions.

1) The state gained control over the art market in Shanghai by building state museums and co-opting con-noisseurs and their art collections; 2) However, state control over the art trade was far from complete; 3) To crack down on illegal trade in antiquities, the Shanghai Cultural Bureau launched a Five-Ants Campaign in 1965 to punish art speculators; 4) Through its cultural institutions, the state controlled art but did not monopolise it.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the Chinese state gained control over the art market in Shanghai during the 195os and 1960’s.
how the state and the market interacted in the realm of art collecting and how the state used cultural institutions to control culture.
how the state and the public interacted with the art world, and how this relationship was shaped by political and economic factors in a socialist society.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the state and the connoisseurs were both in the process of reforming their connoisseurship, and the relationship between them was in a constant process of negotiation and compromise.
the state and collectors in Shanghai during the 195os and 1960’s were both reformers.
connoisseurs in Shanghai in the early PRC were not only the victims but also the beneficiaries of the state’s efforts to reform connoisseurship.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the state’s control over art and connoisseurs was incomplete.
the state’s relationship with art collectors was one of negotiation, rather than control.
the state was a reforming connoisseur.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the state did not have a monopoly on art collecting, but rather coexisted with private collecting.
the state and art collecting were not in a zero-sum relationship.
, in order to understand how the state controlled culture, one needs to examine the relationship between state and non-state actors.
